extracted.intended_audience: general public; fans and researchers of comedy/entertainment
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography summarizing Jeff Ross's life, career (stand-up, roasts, TV/film, voice work), notable roles, genres, subjects he covers, and major appearances/controversies. The page is a factual overview rather than a how-to or evaluation guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres: Observational comedy, insult comedy, black comedy, cringe comedy, satire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists these genres as Jeff Ross's primary comedic styles; they indicate the stylistic registers he works in across stand-up, roasts, specials, and TV appearances. (Verbatim from infobox: 'Genres: Observational comedy, insult comedy, black comedy, cringe comedy, satire')

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects / Thematic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects: American politics, Jewish culture, popular culture, self-deprecation, sex, current events, religion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics are noted as recurring themes in Ross's material and roasts, informing the content choices and targets of his jokes. (Verbatim from infobox: 'Subjects: American politics, Jewish culture, popular culture, self-deprecation, sex, current events, religion')

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing roast jokes and staging a roast
rubrics_metrics.description: Ross published I Only Roast the Ones I Love: Busting Balls Without Burning Bridges in 2009, which 'recounts his journey to becoming Roastmaster General and includes tips on writing roast jokes and how to put on a roast.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references the book as a source of practical tips for composing roast material and organizing roasts, but does not reproduce the tips on-page. Use the book for concrete guidance on technique, tone, and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast Battle competition & judging format
rubrics_metrics.description: The show consists of comedians competing in one-on-one roast battles where the winners are decided by Ross and a panel of guest judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a competitive format for roast performance: head-to-head comedic insults judged by a central figure (Ross) and guest judges. The page states the structure but does not provide explicit scoring criteria or judging rubric (winners are 'decided by Ross and a panel').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of provocative/edgy costumes and material
rubrics_metrics.description: Ross became known for dressing up in edgy and sometimes controversial costumes (examples: roasted Charlie Sheen dressed as Muammar Gaddafi; Rob Lowe dressed as Purple Rain–era Prince shortly after the musician's death; Roseanne Barr roasted dressed as Joe Paterno during the Penn State child sex abuse scandal; James Franco roasted wearing cornrows and a neck tattoo referencing a film role).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides examples showing that provocative visual choices and controversial topical references are part of Ross's roast style. These choices can elevate a roast but also risk controversy or backlash (examples on-page illustrate both impact and potential critique).
